newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank to continue tighten liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank to continue tighten liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Monday it would continue to tighten liquidity in an apparant effort to cool the red-hot stock market, despite persistently high short-term interest rates.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung told reporters that recent interest rate hikes were the result of the stock market rally that has seen the Taiwan share index rise 23.5 percent in 1997 alone.
"Liquidity has flown into a certain market to cause recent surges of short-term interest rates," Hsu said.

"The central bank cannot intervene as to where the funds flow, but it will continue to observe and adjust the situation," Hsu said, indicating the bank would continue to issue negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up banking system liquidity.
"We will control the quantity (of funds)," Hsu said, adding the central bank could tolerate higher interest rates.
The central bank had repeatedly issued NCDs in recent sessions in a strategy widely seen as aiming to cool down the sizzling stock market.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 6.081 percent on Monday, with 30-day short-term commercial paper at 6.00, lower than in recent sessions but still well above the central bank's target zone of 5.00-5.50 percent.
On Monday, Taiwan share prices surged through resistance at 8,400 points to yet another six-year high on huge turnover of T$176.88 billion.
Some analysts have said the stock rally was driven by loose liquidity, rather than reflecting fundamental equity value.
